aliases.reason: The finite-field and prime-field characteristic sources both use a prime positive integer p>1, whose only positive divisors are 1 and p; this is ordinary integer primality, not the different notions of prime ideal or prime-power cardinality.

The clopen-spectrum source's D(e) is the distinguished principal open D(f) of Spec(R) specialized to an idempotent element e. Idempotence makes this open also closed but must remain a source-specific additional hypothesis.

Nonnegatively graded rings and ℤ-graded modules both use an internal additive-group direct-sum decomposition with unique finitely supported homogeneous components. Nonnegative-versus-integer index grading and multiplication/module compatibility are separate parent-specific data.
